# Lab 17.19: Enable Autokey

## What We Are Going to Do
Turn on Cloud KMS Autokey for a folder, so CMEK keys are created automatically when developers create resources.

## Steps

1. **Prepare a folder and a key project.** Create a folder `autokey-lab` and two projects in it: `keys-XXXX` (holds the keys) and `app-XXXX` (holds the resources). Link both to billing.

2. **Set up the key project.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable cloudkms.googleapis.com --project=KEY_PROJECT_ID
gcloud beta services identity create --service=cloudkms.googleapis.com --project=KEY_PROJECT_NUMBER
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding KEY_PROJECT_ID \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.admin \
  --member=serviceAccount:service-KEY_PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-cloudkms.iam.gserviceaccount.com</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **Enable Autokey on the folder.** Create `autokey-config.yaml`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • YAML
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">name: folders/FOLDER_NUMBER/autokeyConfig
keyProject: projects/KEY_PROJECT_ID</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud kms autokey-config update autokey-config.yaml</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Or in the console: **Security → Key Management → Autokey**, select the folder, choose the key project, and enable.

4. **Let developers request keys.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud resource-manager folders add-iam-policy-binding FOLDER_NUMBER \
  --member=group:gcp-developers@YOUR_DOMAIN --role=roles/cloudkms.autokeyUser</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **Create a bucket with Autokey.** In the `app` project, go to **Cloud Storage → Create bucket**. Under **Data encryption**, choose **Cloud KMS key**, then **Cloud KMS with Autokey**. Create the bucket.

6. **See the key.** In the key project, open **Key Management**. A key ring and key were created for you in the bucket's location, with rotation already set.

7. **Clean up.** Delete the bucket. Keys cannot be deleted, but they cost very little. Delete the two projects when you finish this section.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Key creation | Automatic, on demand |
| Key location | Matches the resource |
| Rotation | Set by default |
| Separation | Keys live in a separate key project |
